correctness.rationale: Over F2 the XOR step equals multiplication by f=z+z^{-1}+z^n on F2[z]/(z^(2n)+1). Its only possible zero-primary factor is h=z²+z+1 when 3|n; h has exponent 2e. For n odd the multiplier vanishes on the full h² quotient, yielding four size-one binary blocks. For n even h divides its polynomial numerator simply, giving two chains of length 2e. CRT separates an invertible complementary component and gives exactly P=2^(2n-4e) recurrent states. Differences of kernel dimensions prove all entry shells. Separate gcd and (z+1)-valuation computations prove the fixed-point and primitive-orbit formulas. Direct graph-matrix rank checks passed 1115 cases; 429 independent prism comparisons and exhaustive classification of 87360 states on six graph sizes also passed. Finite cases do not constitute the infinite proof.

value.rationale: A natural Möbius twist of a cyclic three-regular ladder leaves the binary neighbor-XOR recurrent population invariant but dramatically changes its nilpotent Jordan partition and first-entry times. Across infinitely many 3-divisible half-lengths, the even case doubles the sharp maximal transient from e to 2e while the odd case halves it from 2 to 1. The closed shell populations and exact fixed-point trichotomy answer motivated structural and dynamical questions beyond a generic algorithm or finite table.
